svg.aria-label: How to write こんにちは: 5 letters, こ, ん, に, ち, は, one after another
svg.title: Writing こんにちは
svg.desc: 5 letters written one after another: こ, ん, に, ち, は (japanese). Each letter has its own group of frames; frame N of a group shows movements 1 to N of that letter, the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansJP-Subset.ttf. Each letter is drawn at its own scale from its own cited stroke order, so the strip does not show how large the letters are next to each other, how far apart they sit, or any join between them. Stroke order: こ: KanjiVG, kanji/03053.svg, hiragana こ (U+3053 HIRAGANA LETTER KO), two stroke paths kvg:03053-s1 and s2 (Ulrich Apel and contributors, CC BY-SA 3.0) <https://github.com/KanjiVG/kanjivg/blob/master/kanji/03053.svg>; ん: KanjiVG, kanji/03093.svg, hiragana ん (U+3093 HIRAGANA LETTER N), one stroke path kvg:03093-s1 (Ulrich Apel and contributors, CC BY-SA 3.0) <https://github.com/KanjiVG/kanjivg/blob/master/kanji/03093.svg>; に: KanjiVG, kanji/0306b.svg, hiragana に (U+306B HIRAGANA LETTER NI), three stroke paths kvg:0306b-s1 to s3 (Ulrich Apel and contributors, CC BY-SA 3.0) <https://github.com/KanjiVG/kanjivg/blob/master/kanji/0306b.svg>; ち: KanjiVG, kanji/03061.svg, hiragana ち (U+3061 HIRAGANA LETTER TI), two stroke paths kvg:03061-s1 and s2 (Ulrich Apel and contributors, CC BY-SA 3.0) <https://github.com/KanjiVG/kanjivg/blob/master/kanji/03061.svg>; は: KanjiVG, kanji/0306f.svg, hiragana は (U+306F HIRAGANA LETTER HA), three stroke paths kvg:0306f-s1 to s3 (Ulrich Apel and contributors, CC BY-SA 3.0) <https://github.com/KanjiVG/kanjivg/blob/master/kanji/0306f.svg>. Source notes on variation: こ: KanjiVG stores each stroke as one directed path in writing order: s1 is the upper stroke drawn left to right, ending in a small turn down and back to the left that the print glyph does not show; s2 starts at the left, curves down and runs out to the right along the base, rising slightly at its end. Only the order and direction are taken from that file. The learner path's coordinates are the bundled Noto Sans JP outline's own medial line, so the print glyph's proportions, not KanjiVG's handwriting-style ones, decide where each stroke runs. ん: KanjiVG stores ん as one directed path in writing order: it starts at the top, cuts down to the lower left, turns back up the same line, arches over a small hump, comes down, rounds the foot and rises to the right. Only the order and direction are taken from that file. The learner path's coordinates are the bundled Noto Sans JP outline's own medial line, so the print glyph's proportions, not KanjiVG's handwriting-style ones, decide where each stroke runs. In the print glyph the hump leaves the diagonal partway up, so the path goes down to the tip of the diagonal and climbs back up that ink to the branch before turning over the hump. に: KanjiVG stores each stroke as one directed path in writing order: s1 is the left vertical drawn top to bottom, which turns at its foot and flicks up to the right without lifting; s2 is the upper stroke drawn left to right, ending in a small turn down and back to the left that the print glyph does not show; s3 starts at the left, curves down and runs out to the right along the base, rising slightly at its end. Only the order and direction are taken from that file. The learner path's coordinates are the bundled Noto Sans JP outline's own medial line, so the print glyph's proportions, not KanjiVG's handwriting-style ones, decide where each stroke runs. Where the print glyph's left vertical runs on below the point the flick leaves it, the path goes down to the foot of that ink and climbs back a short way before the flick. ち: KanjiVG stores each stroke as one directed path in writing order: s1 is the bar drawn left to right, rising slightly; s2 starts above the bar, falls through it to the lower left, turns sharply back up to the right, rounds the belly on the right and finishes low, heading left. Only the order and direction are taken from that file. The learner path's coordinates are the bundled Noto Sans JP outline's own medial line, so the print glyph's proportions, not KanjiVG's handwriting-style ones, decide where each stroke runs. The print glyph's descender and rising stroke meet in a sharp point, so the path goes down to that tip and turns back up the same ink. は: KanjiVG stores each stroke as one directed path in writing order: s1 is the left vertical drawn top to bottom, which turns at its foot and flicks up to the right without lifting; s2 is the bar drawn left to right; s3 starts above the bar, runs down through it, rounds to the left at its foot, comes back up, crosses the vertical and runs out to the lower right. Only the order and direction are taken from that file. The learner path's coordinates are the bundled Noto Sans JP outline's own medial line, so the print glyph's proportions, not KanjiVG's handwriting-style ones, decide where each stroke runs. Where the print glyph's left vertical runs on below the point the flick leaves it, the path goes down to the foot of that ink and climbs back a short way before the flick.
svg.text: How it is written — 5 letters, one after another
Letter 2 of 5 — one unbroken stroke · 4 movements
Letter 3 of 5 — 3 strokes · 2 pen lifts · 4 movements
Letter 4 of 5 — 2 strokes · 1 pen lift · 4 movements
Letter 5 of 5 — 3 strokes · 2 pen lifts · 6 movements
Letter 1: stroke order after KanjiVG, kanji/03053.svg, hiragana こ (U+3053 HIRAGANA LETTER KO), two stroke paths kvg:03053-s1 and s2 (Ulrich Apel and contributors, CC BY-SA 3.0)
Letter 2: stroke order after KanjiVG, kanji/03093.svg, hiragana ん (U+3093 HIRAGANA LETTER N), one stroke path kvg:03093-s1 (Ulrich Apel and contributors, CC BY-SA 3.0)
Letter 3: stroke order after KanjiVG, kanji/0306b.svg, hiragana に (U+306B HIRAGANA LETTER NI), three stroke paths kvg:0306b-s1 to s3 (Ulrich Apel and contributors, CC BY-SA 3.0)
Letter 4: stroke order after KanjiVG, kanji/03061.svg, hiragana ち (U+3061 HIRAGANA LETTER TI), two stroke paths kvg:03061-s1 and s2 (Ulrich Apel and contributors, CC BY-SA 3.0)
Letter 5: stroke order after KanjiVG, kanji/0306f.svg, hiragana は (U+306F HIRAGANA LETTER HA), three stroke paths kvg:0306f-s1 to s3 (Ulrich Apel and contributors, CC BY-SA 3.0)
This order is attested, not standardised; the source records where it varies.
